question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct regarding the rabi crops?
option_1: Southern and southeastern states are important for the production of wheat and other rabi crops.
option_2: These crops are harvested in summer from April to June.
option_3: Some of the important rabi crops are wheat, barley, peas, gram and mustard.
option_4: Rabi crops are sown in winter from October to December.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Southern and southeastern states are important for the production of wheat and other rabi crops.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rabi crops are agricultural crops that are sown in winter (October to December) and harvested in summer (April to June); they rely on winter rainfall brought by western temperate cyclones for growth. (रबी फसल — शीतकालीन फसल)

 

• Important rabi crops include wheat, barley, peas, gram (chana) and mustard.

 

• Rabi crops (especially wheat) are grown predominantly in the northern and north-western states of India — Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and Rajasthan — not in the southern or south-eastern states.

 

• Because production is concentrated in the north/north-west rather than the south/south-east, the statement that "southern and south-eastern states are important for the production of wheat and other rabi crops" is factually incorrect.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kharif crops (e.g., rice, maize, cotton, jute) are sown with the onset of the monsoon (June–July) and harvested in September–October, the opposite cycle of rabi crops.

 

• Punjab and Haryana together are often called the "wheat bowl" of India due to their leading share in wheat production.

 

NOTE

 

• These crops are harvested in summer from April to June. (Option 2): This is a correct statement about rabi crops — hence not the answer.

 

• Some of the important rabi crops are wheat, barley, peas, gram and mustard. (Option 3): This is a correct statement about rabi crops — hence not the answer.

 

• Rabi crops are sown in winter from October to December. (Option 4): This is a correct statement about rabi crops — hence not the answer.

question:
Which of the following pairs is correct regarding the East India Company army?
I. Sawar – Men on horses
II. Musket – A heavy gun used by infantry soldiers
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the terminology used for the East India Company's army, a Sawar referred to cavalrymen — soldiers who fought on horseback. (सवार — घुड़सवार सैनिक)

 

• A Musket was a heavy gun fired from the shoulder, used by infantry soldiers (foot soldiers) of the Company's army.

 

• The Company's army (the Sepoy Army) was organised into three wings — infantry (foot soldiers), cavalry (Sawars) and artillery — each using distinct weaponry suited to their role.

 

• Since both statement I (Sawar – men on horses) and statement II (Musket – a heavy gun used by infantry soldiers) are historically accurate, both are correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• A Sepoy was the term used for an ordinary Indian infantry soldier recruited into the Company's army.

 

• Over time, the Company's army evolved from primarily cavalry-based Mughal-style forces to a more infantry- and artillery-heavy force trained in European drill.

 

NOTE

 

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, because statement II is also correct — a musket was indeed a heavy gun used by infantry.

 

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect, because statement I is also correct — a Sawar was indeed a man on horseback (cavalryman).

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, because both statements are factually accurate.

question: Which of the following is related to the concurrent list of the seventh schedule of the Indian constitution?
option_4: Taxes on income other than agricultural income.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Factories.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution divides legislative subjects among the Union List, State List and Concurrent List. (सातवीं अनुसूची — संघ, राज्य व समवर्ती सूची)

 

• "Factories" (regulation of labour and safety in factories) is listed as Entry 36 of the Concurrent List, on which both Parliament and State Legislatures can legislate.

 

• Taxes on agricultural income (Entry 46) and Tolls (Entry 59) fall under the State List, over which only State Legislatures can legislate.

 

• Taxes on income other than agricultural income (Entry 82) fall under the Union List, over which only Parliament can legislate.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Concurrent List originally had 47 subjects (now 52 after later amendments) and includes items like Criminal Law, Marriage and Divorce, Education, and Forests.

 

• In case of a conflict between a Union law and a State law on a Concurrent List subject, the Union law generally prevails (Article 254).

 

NOTE

 

• Taxes on agricultural income (Option 1): This falls under the State List, not the Concurrent List.

 

• Tolls (Option 2): This falls under the State List, not the Concurrent List.

 

• Taxes on income other than agricultural income. (Option 4): This falls under the Union List, not the Concurrent List.

question: As on 1st November 2022, who is the chairperson of SEBI’s Market Data Advisory Committee (MDAC)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is M.S. Sahoo.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India) restructured its Market Data Advisory Committee (MDAC) in 2022, expanding it to 20 members.

 

• Dr. M.S. Sahoo, former Chairperson of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI), was appointed as the Chairperson of the MDAC.

 

• The MDAC advises SEBI on policy matters relating to access to and dissemination of securities market data.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India) is the statutory regulator for the securities market in India, established in 1988 and given statutory powers in 1992 under the SEBI Act.

 

• As of the exam period, SEBI's Chairperson was Madhabi Puri Buch.

 

NOTE

 

• Suresh N Patel (Option 1): Not associated with the MDAC as chairperson; he has served in other regulatory/committee roles.

 

• K.V. Kamath (Option 3): A veteran banker who has chaired other bodies (e.g., NaBFID, National Infrastructure Pipeline), but not the MDAC.

 

• Ajay Tyagi (Option 4): A former Chairperson of SEBI itself (2017–2022), not the head of the MDAC.

question: An isotope of which of the following is used in the treatment of cancer?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cobalt.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Cobalt-60, a radioactive isotope of cobalt, emits gamma rays and is widely used in radiotherapy machines ("cobalt units") for the treatment of cancer. (कोबाल्ट-60 — कैंसर चिकित्सा में प्रयुक्त)

 

• Cobalt-60 therapy (teletherapy) is used to destroy or shrink malignant tumours by directing focused gamma radiation at them.

 

• Besides medicine, Cobalt-60 is also used in industrial radiography and for sterilising medical equipment and food.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other radioactive isotopes used in medicine include Iodine-131 (thyroid disorders) and Technetium-99m (diagnostic imaging).

 

• Cobalt itself is a hard, silvery-grey transition metal, atomic number 27, used in making alloys, magnets and batteries.

 

NOTE

 

• Aluminium (Option 2): A lightweight, non-radioactive metal used mainly in packaging, construction and aircraft; not used in cancer treatment.

 

• Nickel (Option 3): A metal chiefly used in alloys (e.g., stainless steel) and batteries; not associated with cancer treatment.

 

• Iron (Option 4): An essential element for haemoglobin in the body and used extensively in construction and industry; not used to treat cancer.

question: How many non-major (minor) ports are there in India as on 31st October 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 200.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's ports are classified into Major Ports, which are administered by the Central Government, and Non-Major (Minor/Intermediate) Ports, which are administered by the respective State Governments.

 

• As on 31st October 2022, India had 13 Major Ports and more than 200 Non-Major (minor/intermediate) Ports. (लघु बंदरगाह)

 

• Non-major ports mainly handle coastal cargo, fishing and small-scale trade, and are regulated under state maritime boards.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The reclassification of Ennore as Kamarajar Port and subsequent additions took India's major port count to 13.

 

• The Sagarmala Programme, launched in 2015, aims to modernise India's ports (major and non-major) and boost coastal shipping and port-led development.

 

NOTE

 

• 154 (Option 1): An understated figure; India's non-major ports as of the reference date numbered more than this.

 

• 168 (Option 2): An understated figure; India's non-major ports as of the reference date numbered more than this.

 

• 246 (Option 4): An overstated figure compared to the officially cited count of about 200 non-major ports as of 31st October 2022.

question: Who won the best actress award in the NEXA International Indian Film Academy Awards 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kriti Sanon.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The NEXA IIFA (International Indian Film Academy) Awards 2022 (22nd IIFA Awards) were held in Abu Dhabi in June 2022, honouring Hindi films of 2021.

 

• Kriti Sanon won the Best Actress award for her performance in the film "Mimi" (2021). (कृति सेनन — सर्वश्रेष्ठ अभिनेत्री)

 

• Vicky Kaushal won the corresponding Best Actor award for "Sardar Udham", and "Shershaah" was declared the Best Film.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• IIFA Awards are one of the most prominent annual award ceremonies for Bollywood (Hindi cinema), traditionally held outside India.

 

• Kriti Sanon received widespread acclaim for her performance in Mimi, in which she played a surrogate mother.

 

NOTE

 

• Jhanvi Kapoor (Option 2): An actress active in Bollywood but was not the Best Actress winner at the NEXA IIFA Awards 2022.

 

• Alia Bhatt (Option 3): A leading Bollywood actress but did not win Best Actress at this particular ceremony.

 

• Deepika Padukone (Option 4): A prominent Bollywood actress but was not the Best Actress winner at the NEXA IIFA Awards 2022.

question: Indian Army’s 1st women combat aviator is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Abhilasha Barak.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Captain Abhilasha Barak became the Indian Army's first woman combat aviator when she was inducted into the Army Aviation Corps in 2021. (भारतीय सेना की प्रथम महिला युद्धक विमान चालक)

 

• She, along with other women officers, was trained to fly the Advanced Light Helicopter (ALH) Rudra, a weaponised platform, marking a historic step for women in combat roles in the Indian Army.

 

• This achievement came after the Indian Army opened up combat aviation roles to women officers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lieutenant General Punita Arora was the first woman Lieutenant General in the Indian Armed Forces and the first woman Vice Admiral in the Indian Navy.

 

• India has progressively opened more combat and command roles to women across the Army, Navy and Air Force in recent years, including permanent commissions.

 

NOTE

 

• Punita Arora (Option 1): The first woman Lieutenant General in the Indian Army/first woman Vice Admiral in the Navy, not the first woman combat aviator.

 

• Divya Ajit Kumar (Option 2): Not recorded as the Indian Army's first woman combat aviator.

 

• Priya Semwal (Option 4): Not recorded as the Indian Army's first woman combat aviator.

question: Raja Parba, also known as Mithuna Sankranti, is a ______ -day-long festival of womanhood celebrated in Odisha, India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is three.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Raja Parba (also called Mithuna Sankranti) is a three-day-long festival celebrating womanhood, observed mainly in Odisha. (रजा पर्व — ओडिशा का त्योहार)

 

• The three days are traditionally known as Pahili Raja, Mithuna Sankranti (Raja Sankranti), and Bhuin Dahana (Basi Raja), sometimes followed by a fourth day, Vasumati Snana, dedicated to bathing the grinding stone (symbolic of Mother Earth).

 

• The festival marks the onset of the monsoon and celebrates the fertility of women and Mother Earth; during this period, agricultural and household work (like grinding and ploughing) traditionally pauses.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Raja Parba is usually celebrated in mid-June, coinciding with Mithuna Sankranti as per the traditional Odia calendar.

 

• Girls and women wear new clothes, apply alta (red dye) on their feet, and enjoy swings (doli) during the festival.

 

NOTE

 

• five (Option 1): Overstates the traditional duration of Raja Parba, which is three (sometimes counted as four) days.

 

• six (Option 2): Overstates the traditional duration of Raja Parba.

 

• four (Option 3): Some accounts include a fourth day (Vasumati Snana), but the core/standard festival duration cited is three days.

question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding inertia?
I. Inertia is the natural tendency of an object to resist a change in its state of motion or of rest.
II. The mass of an object is a measure of its inertia.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Inertia is the inherent property of a body by virtue of which it resists any change in its state of rest or of uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force — this is essentially Newton's First Law of Motion. (जड़त्व — वस्तु का गुण)

 

• The mass of a body is a quantitative measure of its inertia — heavier (more massive) objects have greater inertia and are harder to accelerate or decelerate.

 

• Both given statements (I and II) correctly describe the concept of inertia as understood in classical mechanics.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Inertia is classified into three types: inertia of rest, inertia of motion, and inertia of direction.

 

• Newton's First Law of Motion is also called the "Law of Inertia".

 

NOTE

 

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, because statement II is also correct — mass is indeed the measure of inertia.

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 2): Incorrect, because both statements are true.

 

• Only II (Option 3): Incorrect, because statement I is also correct — inertia is indeed the tendency to resist change in state of motion or rest.

question: How many gold medals did Maharashtra win in the fourth edition of Khelo India Youth Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 45.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 4th edition of the Khelo India Youth Games (KIYG) 2022 was held in Panchkula/Haryana in June 2022, with Haryana as the host state.

 

• Host state Haryana topped the medal tally, while Maharashtra finished second, winning 45 gold medals (along with 40 silver and 40 bronze, totalling 125 medals). (महाराष्ट्र — दूसरा स्थान)

 

• Maharashtra had been the defending champion from earlier editions of the Games before being overtaken by host Haryana in this edition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Khelo India Youth Games is an annual multi-disciplinary grassroots sports competition in India, first held in 2018 (New Delhi).

 

• Host state Haryana finished with 52 gold medals at KIYG 2022, taking the top position in the medal tally.

 

NOTE

 

• 41 (Option 1): Understates Maharashtra's actual gold medal count of 45 at KIYG 2022.

 

• 38 (Option 2): Understates Maharashtra's actual gold medal count of 45 at KIYG 2022.

 

• 54 (Option 3): Overstates Maharashtra's actual gold medal count; this figure is closer to host Haryana's gold tally.

question: Which of the following is NOT a part of western coastal plains?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Coromandel Coast.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's western coastal plains stretch along the Arabian Sea, from Gujarat to Kerala, and comprise sections such as the Kachchh and Kathiawar coast, Konkan coast (Maharashtra), Kannad (Karnataka) coastal plain, and Malabar coast (Kerala).

 

• The Coromandel Coast, in contrast, lies along the eastern coastline of India (Tamil Nadu and southern Andhra Pradesh), facing the Bay of Bengal, and is therefore part of the eastern coastal plains, not the western coastal plains. (कोरोमंडल तट — पूर्वी तटीय मैदान)

 

• Thus, among the given options, Coromandel Coast is NOT a part of the western coastal plains.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The eastern coastal plains are wider than the western coastal plains and include deltas of major rivers like the Godavari, Krishna, Mahanadi and Kaveri.

 

• The western coastal plains are narrower because the Western Ghats run close to the coast, unlike the Eastern Ghats which lie further inland.

 

NOTE

 

• Konkan (Option 1): A stretch of the western coastal plain along the Maharashtra–Goa coast.

 

• Kannad Plain (Option 3): The Karnataka portion of the western coastal plain.

 

• Malabar coast (Option 4): The Kerala portion of the western coastal plain.

question: Pick the odd one out in Central Processing Unit (CPU) of a computer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Output Unit.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Central Processing Unit (CPU) of a computer, often called its "brain", consists mainly of two functional units — the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) and the Control Unit (CU). (सीपीयू — नियंत्रण एवं गणना इकाई)

 

• The ALU performs all arithmetic and logical operations, while the Control Unit directs and coordinates the operations of the entire computer system.

 

• The Output Unit, however, is not a component of the CPU — it is a separate part of the computer's overall architecture, along with the Input Unit and Memory Unit, that displays or delivers processed results to the user.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Together, the ALU and Control Unit (and often internal registers) constitute the CPU, which works alongside memory (RAM), input devices, and output devices to form a complete computer system.

 

• Examples of output units/devices include monitors, printers and speakers.

 

NOTE

 

• ALU and Control Unit both (Option 1): Both are genuine parts of the CPU, so this is not the "odd one out".

 

• Control Unit (Option 2): A genuine component of the CPU.

 

• ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) (Option 3): A genuine component of the CPU.

question: ______ diseases last for only shorter periods of time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Acute.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Acute diseases are illnesses that last for only a short period of time and usually have a rapid onset, such as the common cold, cough, or typhoid. (तीव्र रोग — अल्पकालिक बीमारी)

 

• They typically appear suddenly, run their course quickly, and the body's immune system deals with them within a limited period, often with treatment.

 

• This is in contrast to diseases that persist for a long time or a lifetime.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chronic diseases (e.g., tuberculosis, elephantiasis, arthritis) last for a long duration — months to years — and can have long-term, cumulative effects on health.

 

• Diseases are also broadly classified as infectious (caused by pathogens, communicable) and non-infectious/degenerative (non-communicable).

 

NOTE

 

• Hereditary (Option 1): Diseases passed on from parents to offspring through genes (e.g., haemophilia, colour blindness); duration is not the defining feature.

 

• Chronic (Option 2): Diseases that last for a long period of time, the opposite of what the question describes.

 

• Genetic (Option 4): Diseases caused by abnormalities in an individual's genetic material; duration is not the defining feature.

question: In which year was the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India set up?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1999.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) was established under the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999, passed by the Indian Parliament. (बीमा विनियामक और विकास प्राधिकरण — 1999)

 

• IRDAI is an autonomous, statutory body tasked with regulating and promoting the insurance and re-insurance industry in India, and protecting the interests of policyholders.

 

• Its head office is located in Hyderabad, Telangana.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• IRDAI replaced the earlier informal regulatory role that was performed directly by the Government of India before liberalisation of the insurance sector.

 

• The insurance sector in India was opened up to private and foreign players following the recommendations of the Malhotra Committee (1994).

 

NOTE

 

• 2011 (Option 2): Not the year of IRDAI's establishment.

 

• 1995 (Option 3): Close to, but not the actual year; the Malhotra Committee's report (recommending reforms) came in 1994, while IRDAI itself was set up under the 1999 Act.

 

• 2002 (Option 4): Not the year of IRDAI's establishment.

question: Which of the following is the largest freshwater lake in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Wular.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Wular Lake, located in Bandipora district, Jammu & Kashmir, is the largest freshwater lake in India. (वुलर झील — भारत की सबसे बड़ी मीठे पानी की झील)

 

• It is formed by the Jhelum River and plays an important role in flood control, fisheries and the region's ecology; it is also a designated Ramsar site (wetland of international importance).

 

• Its size varies seasonally, expanding significantly during the monsoon.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Loktak Lake (Manipur) is the largest freshwater lake in North-East India and is famous for its floating phumdis (islands).

 

• Other notable lakes mentioned — Barapani (Umiam Lake, Meghalaya) and Bhimtal (Uttarakhand) — are also freshwater lakes but smaller in size than Wular.

 

NOTE

 

• Barapani (Option 1): A man-made freshwater lake in Meghalaya, smaller than Wular.

 

• Bhimtal (Option 3): A natural freshwater lake in Uttarakhand, smaller than Wular.

 

• Loktak (Option 4): The largest freshwater lake in North-East India, but smaller than Wular at the national level.

question: LTE technology is used in which of the following generation of wireless technologies?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 4G.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• LTE (Long Term Evolution) is a standard for wireless broadband communication that is widely marketed and recognised as a 4G (fourth-generation) technology. (एलटीई — चौथी पीढ़ी की तकनीक)

 

• LTE was developed to provide significantly higher data speeds and lower latency than earlier 3G networks, enabling services like high-speed mobile internet and video streaming.

 

• In India, LTE-based 4G services were commercially rolled out by telecom operators starting around 2012, with widespread adoption following Reliance Jio's launch in 2016.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• 5G, the next generation after 4G/LTE, was commercially rolled out in India in October 2022, offering even higher speeds and lower latency.

 

• Earlier generations — 1G (analog voice), 2G (digital voice, SMS/GSM) and 3G (mobile internet/data) — each represented major leaps in wireless communication technology.

 

NOTE

 

• 3G (Option 1): The third generation of wireless technology, which enabled mobile internet but preceded LTE/4G.

 

• 2G (Option 2): The second generation of wireless technology, primarily for voice calls and SMS.

 

• 1G (Option 4): The first generation of wireless technology, an analog system used only for voice calls.

question:
Macroeconomics deals with which of the following studies?
I. Reasons behind the unemployment of resources
II. Determination of total output
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Macroeconomics is the branch of economics that studies the economy as a whole, dealing with aggregate variables such as national income, employment, inflation and overall output. (समष्टि अर्थशास्त्र)

 

• It examines the reasons behind the unemployment of resources (why factors of production like labour and capital remain idle) — a key concern first systematically addressed by John Maynard Keynes.

 

• It also studies the determination of total output (national income) in an economy, i.e., how the overall level of production, income and employment is determined.

 

• Since both listed areas fall squarely within the scope of macroeconomics, both statements are correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Macroeconomics contrasts with Microeconomics, which studies individual units like households, firms and specific markets.

 

• Key macroeconomic tools/concepts include GDP, inflation, fiscal policy, and monetary policy.

 

NOTE

 

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, because statement II is also within the scope of macroeconomics.

 

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect, because statement I is also within the scope of macroeconomics.

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 3): Incorrect, because both statements are genuine areas of macroeconomic study.

question: Indian cricket team lost 2021 ICC World Test Championship Final to which country?
solution_text:
The correct answer is New Zealand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The final of the inaugural ICC World Test Championship (2019–2021 cycle) was played between India and New Zealand at the Rose Bowl, Southampton, England, in June 2021.

 

• New Zealand won the final by 8 wickets, becoming the first-ever ICC World Test Championship champions. (न्यूज़ीलैंड — प्रथम विश्व टेस्ट चैंपियनशिप विजेता)

 

• Kane Williamson captained the winning New Zealand side, while Virat Kohli captained India in that final.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The ICC World Test Championship was introduced to give context and a definitive "world champion" to Test cricket rankings.

 

• India reached the final of the second WTC cycle (2021–2023) as well but lost to Australia in June 2023.

 

NOTE

 

• Australia (Option 2): Defeated India in the final of the second WTC cycle (2023), not the 2021 final.

 

• England (Option 3): Hosted the 2021 WTC final at Southampton but did not play in it.

 

• Pakistan (Option 4): Did not feature in the 2021 ICC World Test Championship final.

question: ‘281 and beyond’ is the autobiography of which veteran cricketer?
solution_text:
The correct answer is VVS Laxman.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• ‘281 and Beyond’ is the autobiography of former Indian cricketer VVS Laxman, published in 2013. (वीवीएस लक्ष्मण — आत्मकथा)

 

• The title refers to his celebrated 281-run innings against Australia at Eden Gardens, Kolkata, in 2001, widely regarded as one of the greatest Test innings in cricket history, which helped India win after following on.

 

• The book was co-written with sports journalist R. Kaushik.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• VVS Laxman is renowned for his elegant batting style and his particularly strong record against Australia, earning him the nickname "Very Very Special" Laxman.

 

• Other notable Indian cricketer autobiographies include Sourav Ganguly's "A Century Is Not Enough" and various memoirs by other players.

 

NOTE

 

• Kapil Dev (Option 1): Former India captain and all-rounder; his memoirs are titled differently (e.g., "Straight from the Heart").

 

• Sourav Ganguly (Option 3): Former India captain whose autobiography is titled "A Century Is Not Enough", not "281 and Beyond".

 

• Ajinkya Rahane (Option 4): A former India cricketer, but not the author of "281 and Beyond".

question: In which year was the Citizenship Act passed in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1955.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Citizenship Act, 1955 was enacted by the Indian Parliament to provide for the acquisition and determination of Indian citizenship after the commencement of the Constitution. (नागरिकता अधिनियम, 1955)

 

• It lays down provisions for citizenship by birth, descent, registration, naturalisation, and incorporation of territory, as well as provisions for termination of citizenship.

 

• The Act has been amended several times since, notably by the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 (CAA).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Articles 5 to 11 of the Indian Constitution deal with citizenship provisions at the commencement of the Constitution, while the Citizenship Act, 1955 governs citizenship matters thereafter.

 

• India follows a single citizenship model (unlike countries such as the USA which allow dual state-and-federal citizenship).

 

NOTE

 

• 1951 (Option 1): Not the year the Citizenship Act was passed.

 

• 1959 (Option 3): Not the year the Citizenship Act was passed.

 

• 1964 (Option 4): Not the year the Citizenship Act was passed.

question: ______ is an Act of the Parliament of the United Kingdom that partitioned British India into two new independent dominions of India and Pakistan in 1947.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indian Independence Act.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Independence Act, 1947 was an Act of the Parliament of the United Kingdom that partitioned British India into two new independent dominions — India and Pakistan — with effect from 15th August 1947. (भारतीय स्वतंत्रता अधिनियम, 1947)

 

• It ended British paramountcy over the princely states, leaving them free to accede to either dominion, and provided for the appointment of separate Governors-General for the two dominions.

 

• The Act received royal assent on 18th July 1947.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Indian Independence Act, 1947 was based substantially on the Mountbatten Plan (3 June Plan).

 

• India adopted its own Constitution on 26th January 1950, becoming a sovereign republic and superseding the Government of India Act, 1935, as amended by the Indian Independence Act.

 

NOTE

 

• Rowlatt Act (Option 1): A 1919 Act that allowed indefinite detention without trial to curb revolutionary activities; unrelated to Partition.

 

• Government of India Act (Option 3): The Government of India Act, 1935, provided a framework of provincial autonomy and federal structure but did not partition India.

 

• Pitt's India Act (Option 4): An Act of 1784 that brought the East India Company's administration under greater British government control; unrelated to the 1947 partition.

question: ऑस्ट्रेलियन ओपन 2022 में महिला एकल का खिताब किसने जीता था?
solution_text:
The correct answer is एशले बार्टी.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Australian Open 2022 women's singles title was won by Australian tennis player Ashleigh Barty (एशले बार्टी), who defeated Danielle Collins of the USA in the final.

 

• This was Barty's third Grand Slam singles title (ग्रैंड स्लैम — प्रमुख टेनिस चैंपियनशिप), after the French Open 2019 and Wimbledon 2021, and made her the first Australian woman to win the Australian Open singles title in 44 years.

 

• Shortly after this win, in March 2022, Barty announced her retirement from professional tennis while still ranked World No. 1.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The men's singles title at the Australian Open 2022 was won by Spain's Rafael Nadal, who defeated Daniil Medvedev in a comeback final to claim his 21st Grand Slam title.

 

• The Australian Open is the first Grand Slam tournament of the tennis calendar year, held annually in Melbourne, Australia.

 

NOTE

 

• ऐलेना रबाकिना (Option 2): Elena Rybakina, a Kazakhstani player who won the Wimbledon 2022 women's singles title, not the Australian Open 2022.

 

• ओन्स जेब्युर (Option 3): Ons Jabeur, a Tunisian player who reached Grand Slam finals later in 2022 (Wimbledon and US Open), but was not the Australian Open 2022 winner.

 

• सेरेना विलियम्स (Option 4): Serena Williams, a legendary American player, but she did not win the Australian Open 2022 title.

question: Birju Maharaj was a noted dancer of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Birju Maharaj was one of India's foremost exponents and gurus of Kathak, a classical dance form of North India, belonging to the renowned Kalka-Bindadin Gharana of Lucknow. (कथक — उत्तर भारत का शास्त्रीय नृत्य)

 

• He was a recipient of the Padma Vibhushan (1986) and numerous other honours for his contribution to Kathak, and also composed music and choreographed dance sequences for several Bollywood films.

 

• He passed away in January 2022.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The eight classical dance forms of India are Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), and Sattriya (Assam).

 

• Birju Maharaj choreographed for films such as "Devdas" (2002) and "Bajirao Mastani" (2015).

 

NOTE

 

• Bharatnatyam (Option 1): A classical dance form of Tamil Nadu, not the dance form associated with Birju Maharaj.

 

• Manipuri (Option 2): A classical dance form of Manipur, not associated with Birju Maharaj.

 

• Sattriya (Option 4): A classical dance form of Assam, not associated with Birju Maharaj.

question: Who among the following was famously known as the "The parrot of India"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amir Khusro.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Amir Khusro (1253–1325), a renowned Sufi poet, musician and scholar of the Delhi Sultanate era, was famously known as the "Tuti-e-Hind" (Parrot of India) because of his eloquence and mastery over language and poetry. (अमीर ख़ुसरो — भारत का तोता)

 

• He is credited with pioneering contributions to Hindavi (Hindustani) literature, and is traditionally associated with the development of the qawwali musical genre and instruments such as the sitar and tabla (though the latter attributions are debated by historians).

 

• He served as a court poet under several Delhi Sultanate rulers and was a devoted disciple of the Sufi saint Nizamuddin Auliya.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Amir Khusro wrote in both Persian and Hindavi, and composed riddles (paheliyan) and couplets still popular in India today.

 

• His tomb is located near the Nizamuddin Dargah in Delhi.

 

NOTE

 

• Lata Mangeshkar (Option 2): A legendary Indian playback singer known as the "Nightingale of India", a Bharat Ratna recipient, not "Parrot of India".

 

• Pandit Ravishankar (Option 3): A renowned sitar maestro, but not known by the title "Parrot of India".

 

• Kalidas (Option 4): An ancient Sanskrit poet and playwright, known for works like "Abhijnanashakuntalam", but not called "Parrot of India".
